newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-IN FORM SMOLTZ BLANKS PIRATES WITH FOUR-HITTER.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-IN FORM SMOLTZ BLANKS PIRATES WITH FOUR-HITTER.

text.p: John Smoltz seems to have rediscovered his Cy Young Award-winning form.
Smoltz pitched a four-hitter to help Atlanta recover from a tough four-game series against Florida as the Braves blanked the Pittsburgh Pirates 6-0 on Monday.

Smoltz (10-9), last year's NL Cy Young winner who has struggled this season, walked just two, struck out nine and set down 12 batters in a row from the first to the fifth innings in notching his fifth complete game and second shutout of the season.
"It was a big game for me and a big game for the team," Smoltz said. "Our bullpen needed some rest. I'm just glad I was able to finish what I started."
It was the 11th career shutout but first since April 15 for Smoltz, who allowed just one runner to reach third base.
After exceeding his entire 1996 loss total on July 20, the right-hander is 2-0 with 29 strikeouts in three starts.
Andruw Jones got the big hit for Atlanta, which had dropped three of four to the Marlins in their previous series.
Jones belted a two-run homer in the sixth, giving Atlanta a 3-0 lead and triggering a four-run inning that chased Pittsburgh starter Steve Cooke (8-11).

Jones added an infield single in the seventh and walked and scored in the ninth. Jeff Blauser also had two hits and drove in a run for the Braves, who maintained a 5 1/2-game lead over Florida in the NL East.
Cooke gave up only doubles by Blauser in the third and fifth innings until the Braves broke through in the sixth. He ended up allowing five runs and six hits in five-plus innings.

At Florida, rookie sensation Livan Hernandez won his sixth straight start to remain unbeaten and Bobby Bonilla homered and drove in three runs to pace the Marlins to a 4-1 victory over the Houston Astros.
Hernandez (6-0), who has not allowed more than two runs in any game during his streak, gave up a run and four hits over 7-1/3 innings.
Bonilla opened the scoring in the fourth inning with an RBI single off starter Chris Holt (7-8). With Florida clinging to a 2-1 lead in the sixth, Bonilla belted a two-run homer.
Craig Biggio, who had two of Houston's four hits, doubled and scored on Jeff Bagwell's sacrifice fly in the sixth.
In Cincinnati, J.T. Snow homered twice and drove in a career-high five runs and Kirk Rueter pitched seven strong innings as the San Francisco Giants pounded the Reds 9-1.
With the Giants already leading 4-1, Snow drove a 1-0 pitch from Richie Lewis over the left-field wall for a two-run homer in the seventh. He added a three-run shot off Felix Rodriguez in the ninth.

Rueter (8-5) allowed one run and seven hits, walking none and striking out four to improve to 4-0 lifetime against the Reds. Giovanni Carrara (0-1) gave up four runs and five hits over 5 1/3 innings for the loss.
In Philadelphia, Tyler Green allowed three hits over seven innings and Scott Rolen hit a two-run homer as the Phillies beat the struggling Colorado Rockies 7-3 for their sixth win in seven games.
The Rockies were leading 3-2 in the fifth when Rolen's homer off starter Frank Castillo (8-10) put the Phillies ahead for good.
Green (2-1) gave up three runs with four walks and seven strikeouts. Castillo was roughed up for seven runs and nine hits in 5 1/3 innings as Colorado lost for the fifth time in its last seven games.
In New York, Rick Reed pitched six strong innings for his fifth straight win and Lance Johnson hit two RBI triples and scored a run to lead the Mets to a 4-2 win over the St Louis Cardinals.

Reed (10-4) allowed two runs on Royce Clayton's two-run triple in the second and four hits with no walks and four strikeouts. He left for a pinch hitter in the bottom of the sixth following an 87-minute rain delay.

The Mets, who stayed two games behind Florida in the NL wild card race, spoiled the major-league debut of Miguel Aybar, a converted shortstop who surrendered four runs and seven hits in 5 1/3 innings.
